commander_specific_hypothesis: The Indomitable draws a card whenever a creature you control deals combat damage to a player, matching Coastal Piracy's core trigger. After attacking with at least three tapped Pirates and/or Vehicles, it can be cast from the graveyard for its normal {2}{U}{U} cost; that condition naturally overlaps with Beckett's three-Pirate combat plan.
expected_benefit: Preserves one combat-damage draw slot while adding a 6/6 trample Vehicle that can be crewed, plus a repeatable graveyard-cast line after a wide attack. The candidate is a high-ranked commander-specific candidate (#2) and is present in about 50.4% of the EDHREC sample, with lift score 9.30.
tradeoff: Unlike Coastal Piracy, The Indomitable's draw trigger is mandatory, it is an artifact rather than an enchantment, and its recursion requires three tapped Pirates and/or Vehicles. It is not a free cast from the graveyard; the full mana cost must be paid and normal timing rules apply. Artifact removal is a meaningful vulnerability. Existing Bident of Thassa and Kindred Discovery remain separate draw engines.
oracle_rules_legality_checked: PASS — current Oracle text and Commander legality verified via MTG.WTF card entry for The Indomitable (LCC #75), which reports legal Commander and the 2023-11-10 official rulings; candidate color identity is blue and fits UBR. Coastal Piracy current Oracle text verified in the current deck audit; its optional combat-damage draw trigger is the main point of comparison.
test_plan: No decklist change made. If approved, replace 1x Coastal Piracy with 1x The Indomitable, then recount the exact 100-card list, confirm singleton and UBR color identity, refresh current card metadata, and update the frozen-list hash for the revised candidate list. If declined, retain Coastal Piracy and keep the baseline unchanged.
reviewer_notes: This is a role-for-role comparison rather than a popularity-only addition. The Indomitable's graveyard permission checks only for three tapped Pirates/Vehicles as casting begins; it does not reduce the {2}{U}{U} cost and does not change normal timing. Current list's combat plan regularly taps Pirates to attack, making the condition plausible. Main concern is mandatory draw causing unwanted deck depletion in a wide combat turn; weigh this against the recursive 6/6 trample body. No other candidate cleared the same material-upgrade threshold in this first pass.
